messages:
maria: Quick find: running TP=8 inference with long KV cache (seq 2048) shows ~1.1-1.4GB extra per-GPU attributed to NCCL comm buffers + transient staging slices. Repro attached.

raj: yikes. which runtime/config? nvlink or PCIe? allocator?

maria: nvlink, latest runtime build (main @1956), default staging arena size 256MB, comm chunking set to 32MB. profiler trace below.

oliver: can you paste a small snippet of the profiler numbers? my guess is fragmentation + temp workspace not being recycled between collectives.

maria: sure -- quick excerpt from `ncu` traces + allocator counters:

```text
GPU0 total 32.0GB
  model weights: 12.2GB
  kv cache: 6.8GB
  activations/tmp: 8.5GB
  nccl_comm_tmp: 1.25GB
  allocator_free: 3.45GB
```

nccl_comm_tmp spikes only during the simultaneous all-reduce steps and doesn't get returned to the free pool fast enough. observed similar on A100-80GB but numbers scale.

dana: I can reproduce locally with the repro script. command I used: `python tools/repro_comm_mem.py --tp 8 --seq 2048 --model gpt-small --iters 20`. shows same per-GPU spike around iter 3-4.

raj: two quick hypotheses: 1) NCCL allocator path is allocating per-call buffers (we can instead hand it a pre-allocated buffer), 2) our allocator fragmentation increases when many small shards are requested by tensor-parallel ops.

oliver: agree. also kernel selection interacts: for long seq fallback attention kernels allocate extra workspace for causal masks / fused ops. if kernel picks fallback for seq>1024 you get additional tmp.

maria: patch idea: reserve a comm_scratch pool per-stream at startup and pass pointers into collectives; make it reused across collective calls. also expose `RUNTIME_COMM_CHUNK_BYTES` and `RUNTIME_PREALLOC_COMM` flags.

raj: note: ncclGroupStart()/ncclGroupEnd() helps batching NCCL calls but won't change allocator behavior unless we hand explicit pointers. the prealloc approach should avoid allocator churn. also consider aligning KV shard base to 256KB to reduce small-fragment allocs.

oliver: experiment matrix we should run:
  1) baseline
  2) pre-reserve comm pool (prealloc)
  3) aggressive slab coalescing (merge small free blocks)
  4) reduce comm chunk size to 16MB to force more but smaller allocations
\measure: peak memory per-GPU, throughput, and OOM rate. small script flag `--trace-workspace` to log kernel/workspace variant.

maria: quick numbers from a micro-run with a local prealloc prototype (TP=8, seq=2048, batch=1):

```text
baseline: nccl_comm_tmp peak ~1.25GB, p50 latency 42ms, OOMs 0/20
prealloc-pool: nccl_comm_tmp peak ~0.28GB (moved to prealloc), p50 latency 44ms (+2ms), OOMs 0/20
slab-coalesce: peak ~0.6GB, p50 43ms
reduce-chunk-16MB: peak ~0.9GB, p50 41ms
```

so prealloc wins on peak memory with small latency hit.

dana: nice. can you push the repro + unit tests? I'll run CI-large after the PR. also add quick eval to measure cold-start vs steady-state memory.

maria: will open PR today. one more operational note: Dedicated customers with reserved GPUs may object to prealloc if it increases committed reserved usage. make flag opt-in (default off) and add auto-detect: only prealloc when free_mem >= (model + kv + prealloc_margin).

raj: good call. also check kernel selection heuristics: if we can keep the fused kernels (lower workspace) selected for our long-seq case, we avoid extra allocations. we should log kernel variant and compare.

oliver: I'll add the kernel-variant hook to the runtime tracer. then run the experiment matrix across 4 hardware types (A10, A100-40, A100-80, H100) to ensure generality.

deploy-bot: CI queued: perf/run-comm-mem (1956789120) — estimated 18m.

maria: thanks all. I'll post PR link + perf diffs & a short repro guide in this thread when ready. planning to include: repro script, opt-in prealloc flag, a telemetry metric `comm_prealloc_savings_bytes`.

raj: also add a small test to ensure prealloc path doesn't regress latency SLOs for hosted API. if latency bump >5% fail the gating.

dana: i'll run the prod-like nightly with opt-in on a sample shard to validate.

maria: filing tracking issue now. follow-up: add KV eviction fallback if prealloc not possible (streaming KV eviction to reduce peak).

oliver: sounds good. ping me if you want me to review the PR quick. :thumbsup:
